suggestion.summary: Review Spring datasource configuration for Java 21 / Spring Boot 3 migration
steps: Review datasource URLs and drivers for target runtime

lightspeed.recommendation:
**Remediation plan – “Spring datasource properties detected” (configuration‑management‑0300)** *Target runtime:* **java‑21** – Spring Boot 3.x (Jakarta EE) --- ## 1. Files that must be edited (exact paths & line changes) | File (relative to project root) | Edit type | Exact change (copy‑paste) | |----------------------------------|-----------|---------------------------| | **pom.xml** | • Set Java version to 21
• Upgrade Spring Boot parent to 3.x
• Add/upgrade JDBC drivers that are Java‑21 compatible | ```xml

spring.datasource.employees.driver-class-name=com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver``` | | **src/main/java/***``**/config/CustomersDataSourceConfig.java** *(or the class that creates the “customers” DataSource)* | • Change imports from `javax.*` to `jakarta.*` if present
• Ensure `@ConfigurationProperties(prefix = "spring.datasource.customers")` is present
• Use `DataSourceBuilder.create().type(HikariDataSource.class)` (Hikari is default in Boot 3) | ```java

// Same pattern – only the prefix changes``` | | **Any JPA configuration class** (e.g., `JpaConfig.java`) | • Replace `javax.persistence.*` imports with `jakarta.persistence.*`
• Ensure `EntityManagerFactory` beans reference the correct `DataSource` bean names | ```java

+import jakarta.persistence.EntityManagerFactory;
``` | | **src/main/resources/application‑aamf.properties** (optional) | • If you rely on the default datasource (no custom prefix) remove the custom prefixes or add a “primary” datasource. No code change needed if you already have the two custom datasources. | *No edit required unless you want a primary datasource.* | > **If the project does not contain a `CustomersDataSourceConfig` / `EmployeesDataSourceConfig` class** > Search for any class annotated with `@Configuration` that creates a `DataSource` bean (e.g., `DataSourceConfig`, `MultiDataSourceConfig`). Those are the files you must edit as shown above. --- ## 2. Ordered execution steps for the Coder agent 1. **Upgrade Maven build** ```bash # Ensure Maven uses Java 21 (set JAVA_HOME or use toolchains) export JAVA_HOME=$(dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f $(which java)))) # points to JDK‑21 mvn -N versions:set-property -Dproperty=java.version -DnewVersion=21 ``` 2. **Edit `pom.xml`** (apply the XML snippet above). Commit the change. 3. **Add driver‑class‑name properties** to `src/main/resources/application-aamf.properties` (copy the two lines). 4. **Locate datasource configuration classes** ```bash grep -R "DataSourceBuilder" -n src/main/java | grep -i customers grep -R "DataSourceBuilder" -n src/main/java | grep -i employees ``` For each class found, apply the Java snippet (replace any `javax.*` imports with `jakarta.*` and add `@ConfigurationProperties` with the correct prefix). 5. **Update JPA imports** (if any) from `javax.persistence` → `jakarta.persistence`. ```bash grep -R "javax.persistence" -n src/main/java | cut -d: -f1 | sort -u | while read f; do sed -i 's|javax.persistence|jakarta.persistence|g' "$f" done ``` 6. **Validate the classpath** – run `mvn dependency:tree | grep postgresql` and `| grep mssql-jdbc` to confirm the new driver versions are present. 7. **Compile** ```bash mvn clean compile -DskipTests ``` 8. **Run the test suite with the required profile** ```bash mvn test -Dspring.profiles.active=aamf ``` 9. **If compilation or tests fail** * Examine the error messages for missing driver classes or `ClassNotFoundException`. * Ensure the driver‑class‑name properties match the actual driver classes (`org.postgresql.Driver`, `com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver`). * Verify that any custom `DataSource` beans are annotated with `@Primary` if a single primary datasource is expected. 10. **Commit all changes** and push to the repository. --- ## 3.
